conservatory_theory_exam_pencil.name: conservatory_theory_exam_pencil
conservatory_theory_exam_pencil.description: Music-theory student's #2 HB pencil on bright white printed exam paper with light uneven pressure, slightly shaky stems, oval noteheads, and heavy eraser ghosts.
conservatory_theory_exam_pencil.paleography_notes: Models timed undergraduate harmony and counterpoint exams written with a standard #2/HB wood-cased pencil on bright laser-printed staff paper. Characterized by relatively light graphite density with noticeable pressure dropout and tonal variance, slight exam-nerves stem tremor, rounded-oval noteheads, and frequent eraser smudges from voice-leading corrections alongside Roman-numeral margin annotations.

amateur_gel_pen_black.name: amateur_gel_pen_black
amateur_gel_pen_black.description: Modern 0.5mm black gel pen on bright white blank staff paper with smooth uniform line width, slight ink globs at starts/stops, inconsistent spacing, and cursive-3 or zigzag rests.
amateur_gel_pen_black.paleography_notes: Models everyday home arrangements and songwriting drafts written with a 0.5mm black rollerball gel pen (e.g., Pilot G2 or Muji) on bright white store-bought manuscript pads. High nib_min_ratio reflects the spherical ball tip, elevated ink_pooling captures gel blobs at stroke endpoints and pauses, and uneven horizontal planning yields wide spacing jitter and end-of-bar cramming.

pub_fiddler_pocket_notebook.name: pub_fiddler_pocket_notebook
pub_fiddler_pocket_notebook.description: Traditional folk fiddler's hurried pocket tune book in blue-black ballpoint on cream notebook paper with cramped bars, tilted staves, quick slash rests, and minimal clefs.
pub_fiddler_pocket_notebook.paleography_notes: Models Irish, Scottish, and old-time session tune books jotted rapidly in an A6/A5 cream pocket manuscript notebook with a blue-black ballpoint pen. Features pronounced staff slope and curvature from writing on a knee or uneven table, skipping ballpoint dropout, cramped measures with strong end-bar compression, abbreviated slash noteheads, hurried slash-zig rests, and minimal clefs.

church_organist_hymnal_pencil.name: church_organist_hymnal_pencil
church_organist_hymnal_pencil.description: Church organist's neat soft-pencil four-part harmonization with compact vertical chords, gentle right lean, clean round noteheads, and soft graphite grain.
church_organist_hymnal_pencil.paleography_notes: Models disciplined four-part SATB descants, reharmonizations, and service preludes written in soft 2B/B graphite on warm cream manuscript paper. Emphasizes tight vertical chord alignment with low spacing jitter, compact well-closed noteheads, gentle forward slant, rich toothy graphite grain, neat classical clefs, and moderate registration/pedal pencil notes in the margins.

lefthand_smudged_graphite.name: lefthand_smudged_graphite
lefthand_smudged_graphite.description: Left-handed music student's back-slanted -11 deg pencil hand with graphite palm smudging, uneven bar widths, and hurried hooked rests.
lefthand_smudged_graphite.paleography_notes: Models a left-handed student writing in HB/2B pencil with a characteristic -11 degree backward slant, reversed nib orientation, and downward-leftward staff slope. High eraser_smudge_prob and graphite grain capture the classic left-hand palm smudge across freshly penciled measures, paired with irregular bar widths and rapid backwards-7 hooked rests.

rehearsal_black_ink_bold.name: rehearsal_black_ink_bold
rehearsal_black_ink_bold.description: Choir or band director's bold dark rollerball on photocopied blank staff paper with heavy high-contrast lines, bold overshooting barlines, and slightly cramped phrase endings.
rehearsal_black_ink_bold.paleography_notes: Models quick vocal warm-ups, brass cuts, and rehearsal inserts written by a choir or band director with a bold 1.0mm black rollerball or sign pen on photocopied blank staff paper. High contrast between near-black ink and crisp dark photocopied staves, heavy stroke_scale, large legible oval noteheads, emphatic overshooting barlines, and dense rehearsal cues in the margins.
